text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Bund futures remained in positive territory most of the day but well within recent ranges as traders readied for key economic indicators later in the week. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.41, up 0.05 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts ended 3/32 lower on the day. Traders said the morning's gains were not based on solid buying and quickly proved unsustainable. All eyes on M4, CBI industrial trends survey and auction announcement on Tuesday. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-29/32, down 3/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures slipped back in a quiet session after failing to set new highs early on and settled unchanged ahead of potentially market moving events in the United States and Germany on Tuesday. The March bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.48, down 0.2 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures held at firmer levels after touching new record highs in early trading, helped by the strength of other European debt markets, while support also came from a stronger lira and dollar. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 131.60, up 0.28 from Friday's settlement price.
UNITED STATES - The U.S. Treasury market was closed on Monday for the Martin Luther King Day holiday. Trading will resume on Tuesday.
In a shortened session on Friday in New York, the key 6-1/2 percent 30-year bond ended up 1/32 at 95-26/32 to yield 6.83 percent.
JAPAN - Key March Japanese government bond futures ended with marked gains following a plunge in Tokyo stocks.
In after-hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.27, up 0.62 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - With the mainstream dollar market closed due to a U.S. holiday, the Eurobond market focused on European currencies and investors. Three sterling deals surfaced.

University of Harvard made a rare appearance in the market with a 75 million sterling ($125 million) three-year bond which paid 15 basis points over gilts. GMAC followed with a 150 million sterling three-year issue which offered a 41 basis point spread.
Later in the session BAA Plc launched a 200 million sterling 10-year bond via HSBC Markets and BZW, which will be priced to yield 46 basis points over gilts. ($1=.6021 Sterling)
